title: artifact-runtime-contract-v2
description: What downstream execution offers a package: the deliveries it can send, its turn and time limits, the setup operations it may run, what it observes during a run, and the target's seed slots. Authoring is target-free, so this contract is all it knows about execution. The orchestrator writes one contract per target, and generate --runtime-contract validates the file against this schema before any model request.

authoring_transports.description: The connections authoring has. Each is unavailable: authoring never reaches discovery, a judge, setup, or the target.

delivery.description: How execution can send the stimulus: one direct user message, sequential user turns, or a planted item that the target returns from a tool call. Every contract offers the direct user message.

max_planned_turns.description: The most user turns a package may plan.

observation.description: What execution captures during a run. Without claim_levels, a package may claim only command_attempt or reply.

setup_permissions.description: The target operations a package may run as setup before the stimulus.

seed_slots.description: The fields of the target's records that can hold the text of a planted_item delivery.

seed_slot.description: One field of the target's records that can hold planted text, and how the target writes the text there.

carrier_operation.description: The operation whose result returns the field to the agent.

field.description: Where the planted text sits in the carrier's result.

controller.description: Who could have written the field, in the scenario-handoff's terms.

content_kind.description: What the field holds, in the scenario-handoff's terms.

records.description: The records whose field can hold the planted text.

max_chars.description: The most characters of planted text the target accepts in this field.

mode.description: How the target writes the planted text: replace swaps the field's text for it; append adds it after the field's text, which keeps a record that is found by words in its text findable.
